evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14368.txt (sha256 7e7fdf3f... verified; all 17 clause spans and the whole-text quote match the bytes)
jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv and EVENT_CANDIDATES.csv rows for EO:14368 (5 U.S.C. 5332 note)
cruden number EO:14368 (12 matches in 3 files)
reasons: Identity (EO 14368, December 18, 2025, 90 FR 60521, Adjustments of Certain Rates of Pay) and all quoted spans check against the held text, and the clause inventory covers sections 1 to 8. The YES outcome is plausible because no held instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order before 2026-10-14 and the U.S. Code prints it under 5 U.S.C. 5332. The claim is rejected because it states that no held source shows performance of section 5(b)'s Federal Register publication duty and that the OPM notice is not held, while the checkout holds the OPM notice of February 3, 2026, which says in terms that its publication satisfies section 5(b). The publication command was performed on that date and needs to be recorded (split from the continuing duty to take implementing actions, or recorded as a performed later event); the search and rationale text must also be corrected. The section 4 law-enforcement assessment directive is not addressed by that notice, so its operative recording stands on the held record.

evidence_checked: jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12908.txt (sha256 d7cc1976... verified; all 10 clause spans match)
jobs/current-law/output/MENTIONS.csv rows for EO:12908 (5 U.S.C. 3345 note table; 10 U.S.C. 7013, 7015, 7017 notes)
cruden number EO:12908 (own FR printing and GPO FR text only)
grep of jobs/*/output/texts for later Army succession instruments (none beyond the order's own printings)
reasons: Identity checks: EO 12908 of April 22, 1994, Order of Succession of Officers To Act as Secretary of the Army, 59 FR 21907, FR Doc. 94-10241. All quotes match the held bytes. The ten clauses cover section 1(a) with its three positions, 1(b) with its two subparagraphs, 1(c), 1(d) and section 2, so the inventory is complete. The order has no own-terms end or revocation clause. The cruden search and a text search for later Army succession orders or memoranda found nothing beyond the order's own printings. The OFR catalog gives no disposition note. The current U.S. Code (release point 119-121) lists EO 12908 in the 5 U.S.C. 3345 note table of orders of succession and cites it in the 10 U.S.C. 7013, 7015 and 7017 notes without any revocation mark, which supports a continuing predicate through the cutoff. The claim does not discuss the 1998 Federal Vacancies Reform Act's replacement of the cited 5 U.S.C. 3347. That replacement is not shown to have ended the order, and the current 3345 note table treats it as in force, so the omission is not a defect. The savings and search statements are accurate.

evidence_checked: cruden number EO:12261 (own FR printing and 1989 OFR codification only)
reasons: Identity checks: EO 12261 of January 5, 1981, Gasohol in Federal Motor Vehicles, 46 FR 2023, FR Doc. 81-832. All quotes match the held bytes, and paragraphs 1-101 through 1-110(b) are each inventoried, with the preamble correctly treated as non-operative. No held instrument amends or revokes the order. The cruden search finds only the order's own printing and the 1989 codification. The OFR catalog gives no disposition note. The current U.S. Code prints the order under 42 U.S.C. 8871 and still directs procurement 'consistent with Executive Order Number 12261' in 10 U.S.C. 2922c(a), so the predicate for the procurement and delegation clauses is supported through the cutoff. There are two minor points, neither material. First, the rationale's phrase 'report gasohol usage data to the Department of Energy' is a paraphrase without quotation marks; the clause's own judgment reason states the duty correctly as making data available on request. Second, 10 U.S.C. 2922c(a) covers the Secretary of Defense's fuel contracts for other agencies' vehicles. The current status of section 815 of Pub. L. 96-107, which clause 1-105 cross-references, could not be checked from held bytes because no full U.S. Code XML is held. The current Code prints the clause unchanged, so no defect is established.

defects.source_says: EO 13637 is 'Executive Order 13637 of March 8, 2013' (78 FR 16129, March 13, 2013) and the first_end source's own signing_date is 2013-03-08; the clause's judgment_reason and the research_rationale both give 2013-03-08. The first_end date is wrong by three years and inconsistent with the claim's own text.

evidence_checked: jobs/current-law/output/EVENT_CANDIDATES.csv and MENTIONS.csv rows for EO:12423 (22 U.S.C. 2381 and 2751 notes)
reasons: Identity (EO 12423, May 26, 1983, 48 FR 24025, FR Doc. 83-14689) and all quoted spans check against the held bytes, and the two-section inventory is complete. Section 4 of EO 13637 of March 8, 2013 revokes EO 11958 as amended, and the claim's prose correctly dates that revocation 2013-03-08. The structured first_end for section 2, however, gives the date 2010-03-08. That date is wrong and contradicts the claim's own source, judgment reason and rationale, so the claim is rejected. The corrected claim should also take care with EO 12560 section 11 (May 24, 1986). That section amended section 1(d) 'to read as follows', which replaced in full the text that EO 12423 section 2 had inserted. The claim treats this as a non-ending later event under the strike-and-insert ruling, and a corrected claim should state that ruling's application to a full restatement explicitly. Section 1's operative status is not contradicted by any held source.
